questions.q: Why does this lesson say a review board format tests something a written exam answer cannot?
options: Because written answers are always technically wrong
Because review boards never involve any written material at all
Because written exams are easier than any spoken format
Because it tests whether an architect can present a design out loud and hold up their own reasoning under direct, unscripted questioning
questions.explain: The lesson's core distinction is that live defense of a design under pointed, unscripted questioning is a genuinely different skill from producing a correct written answer -- which is why Salesforce's own capstone CTA credential uses a review board format.

questions.q: Which Salesforce architecture credential does this lesson identify as using a review board format for its final evaluation?
options: Salesforce Certified Administrator
Salesforce Certified Platform Developer I
Salesforce Certified Technical Architect (CTA)
Salesforce Certified AI Associate
questions.explain: The lesson identifies the Certified Technical Architect (CTA) credential, Salesforce's capstone above the System Architect and Application Architect tracks, as the one evaluated through a live review board format.

questions.q: What three general phases does this lesson describe a review board format as commonly following?
options: Registration, payment, and certificate issuance
Coding, testing, and deployment
Research, writing, and peer review
Preparation, presentation, and question-and-answer
questions.explain: The lesson describes the general shape as a preparation phase (working through the scenario and producing artifacts), a presentation phase, and a question-and-answer phase where the panel probes the solution.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what specifically should a candidate do when answering a panelist's pointed question about a design choice?
options: Give a generic, unanchored justification that could apply to any scenario
Point back to a specific fact stated in the scenario that justifies the choice, since panelists can't read the candidate's mind and may miss a point made only once
Avoid answering the question directly and change the subject
Insist the panel is wrong to ask the question at all
questions.explain: The lesson's key practice habit is anchoring every answer to a concrete fact from the scenario, since accounts of this format note panelists can't read a candidate's mind and might miss something stated only once in passing.

questions.q: According to this lesson, does Salesforce's own CTA review board format have fixed, unchanging timings and procedures?
options: Yes, the format has never changed since Salesforce introduced it
No -- exact timings and procedural details have changed over time, including a shift to fully virtual delivery, so current official materials should always be checked
The format has no timing structure of any kind
The format is identical to a standard multiple-choice exam
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly notes that exact timings and procedural details for Salesforce's own CTA board have changed over time, including a shift to virtual delivery, and tells students to confirm current details against Salesforce's own official materials rather than relying on this lesson's general description.
